subject: Biotechnology
title: The Promise and Limits of Personalized Medicine
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Promise and Limits of Personalized Medicine usable.

hook.text: Personalized medicine promises the right treatment for each patient — but most prescriptions are still one-size-fits-all.

buildup.text: Genomic data generation far outpaces clinical implementation — hospitals lack infrastructure to use results routinely.

discovery.text: Health disparities widen when genomics serves only wealthy populations — equitable access is an ethical imperative.

twist.text: Common diseases are influenced by environment as much as genetics — genes are just one piece of the puzzle.

climax.text: The vision: every patient's genome in their health record, guiding every medical decision for their entire life.

punchline.text: Personalized medicine is a promise in progress — genomics leads, healthcare follows.

quiz.question: What is the main barrier to widespread personalized medicine adoption?
options: Genomic sequencing is still too expensive for any hospital
Clinical infrastructure and equitable access lag behind the pace of genomic data generation
Patients do not want their genomes sequenced

details.summary: Personalized medicine uses genomic and molecular data to tailor treatment to individual patients. details.whyItMatters: Personalized medicine has achieved remarkable successes but faces real limits. Understanding both the promise and challenges provides a realistic framework for patients and clinicians navigating the genomic medicine revolution without either hype or
takeaways: Targeted cancer therapy and pharmacogenomics are proven personalized medicine successes
Most common diseases remain too complex for simple genomic prediction
Health equity gaps threaten to make personalized medicine benefit only some populations

faq.question: Where has personalized medicine been most successful?
faq.answer: Cancer genomics drives targeted therapy selection with companion diagnostics. Pharmacogenomics prevents adverse drug reactions. Rare disease diagnosis ends years-long diagnostic odysseys. Prenatal screening with NIPT has transformed obstetric care.

faq.question: What are the biggest barriers to widespread personalized medicine?
faq.answer: Lack of diversity in genomic databases excludes non-European populations. Variant interpretation requires specialized expertise in short supply. Healthcare systems lack infrastructure for genomic data integration. Cost and insurance coverage remain barriers.
